text:
sam: FYI I opened a docs PR to expand the Troubleshooting > Errors page: added a short 429 vs 504 section, clarified when to do model fallback vs retry, and updated SDK examples for timeouts. Need eyes on the snippets and the migration note for `backoff_strategy`.

alisha: Looks useful. One quick callout: the old doc linked to `/docs/fallbacks#policy` but that anchor was renamed. We should fix the link and add a redirect note.

noah: I'll fix the link. Also suggest we add a tiny example showing AbortController for JS timeouts so people don't conflate client-side timeout handling with server 504s.

toni: Good idea. For streaming we should show how partial outputs are returned on 429s vs 504s. 429 usually leaves the stream open for a bit then sends a rate-limit final frame; 504 means the server cut the connection. Small note under "Streaming behavior" will help customers debug.

sam: Draft JS timeout snippet (not in PR yet):
```js
// cancel if backend is taking too long locally
const controller = new AbortController();
const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 7000); // 7s client timeout
try {
  await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-large', messages: ctx, signal: controller.signal });
} finally {
  clearTimeout(timer);
}
```

alisha: Nice. For backoff migration, can we include a JSON example of the new shape? People keep searching for the old `retry_policy`.

sam: Added a small migration snippet: `"backoff_strategy": { "type": "exponential", "base_ms": 300, "max_ms": 10000, "jitter": true }` in the PR.

noah: I ran linkcheck locally and it failed on one internal reference. I pushed a commit that updates the anchor and adds a short note: "If you see repeated 429s after switching to backoff_strategy, verify your load-testing clients aren't hammering the key."

toni: Also add a troubleshooting checklist bullet: 1) Check Retry-After header 2) Consider smaller model 3) Trim conversation (drop earliest messages) 4) Use caching or prefix cache for repeated prompts.

sam: For trimming, prefer dropping oldest messages. Adding a small pseudo snippet for trimming tokens rather than messages so it matches tokenized models.

sam: ```py
# pseudo-code: drop oldest tokens until under budget
while tokens(context) + expected_completion_tokens > token_limit:
    context = drop_oldest_token(context)
response = client.generate(model='redwood-chat', messages=context)
```

alisha: One more: can we add a short note about SDKs returning a structured error with `code: "rate_limit"` vs raw HTTP 429? Some users see different shapes depending on the integration.

noah: Good call. I'll standardize examples showing both the HTTP header handling and SDK-level error fields.

docs-bot: PR 7420: CI found a broken anchor in /docs/errors.md :x: (linkcheck)

sam: Fixed and pushed. Re-running CI.

docs-bot: PR 7420: CI passed :white_check_mark:

noah: LGTM, merged after small nit about wording.

toni: Thanks — I'll add a follow-up note in the changelog about the anchor fix so external links don't regress.

sam: Thanks all. I'll also add a tiny section in the SDK migration guide calling out `backoff_strategy` and the common pitfalls (no jitter, too-small base_ms).
